---
title: Check a folder of type definitions before you register them
sidebar_label: Check type definitions
description: Find everything a server would refuse in a folder of type definitions, on your own computer or in a repository's checks, before you register any of them.
job: A builder checks a folder of type definitions against Marfa's registration rules before registering them.
kind: how-to
---

`marfa types check` judges a folder of type definitions by the rules a server applies when it registers a type. **It needs no server, key or sign-in, and sends nothing,** so it runs the same on your computer and in a repository's checks. [Define a type](/build/define-a-type) says what a definition holds.

## Lay out the folder

Put each definition directly in one folder, in a file named for its type's `id`, with its guidance beside it if it has any:

```text
types/
  acme.receipt.json
  acme.receipt.md
  acme.expense-report.json
```

- **`<id>.json`** holds the body `marfa types register --file` sends. A file named for anything else, even in another case, is refused `file_name_mismatch`.
- **`<id>.md`** is the type's guidance, read as `marfa types register` reads it. A Markdown file named for a type with no definition beside it is refused; any other, such as a `README.md`, is left alone.
- **Subfolders, names that start with a dot, and edge types** are not read.

## Run the check

```bash
marfa types check types
```

The check judges each type against the types Marfa ships and the folder's other types, a parent before the types beneath it. **It reports every problem in every file at once,** each with the file, the path in the definition, and the code and message a server would give. `--json` prints `{ ok, checked, refused, files }` for a script to read.

| It exits | When |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | A server would register every file. |
| `1` | A file would be refused, or the folder holds no `.json` file. |
| `2` | The path isn't a folder. |

Once the check passes, register the types, each parent before the types that name it, as [Define a type](/build/define-a-type#register-the-type) shows.

## What the check can't know

**Some rules need an instance.** The check can't tell whether an `id` is already registered, what your key may register, or how large a request the instance takes.

A parent that Marfa doesn't ship and the folder doesn't hold is reported missing, even when your instance has it. A type whose parent is missing, refused or in a loop with it gets the answer a server would give without that parent, with the reason beside it.

The rules are in [Checking a folder of type definitions](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/v0.0.90/conformance/spec/cli.md#checking-a-folder-of-type-definitions) in the contract.
